transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Cora Vauclim and President Trump is campaigning
for Republican candidates two weeks before the midterm elections.
NPR Stephen Fowler reports Trump was in Kansas yesterday and today will go to North Carolina.
On paper, this is not really where the leader of the Republican Party should be spending
his time and energy.
Kansas hasn't elected a Democratic senator in nearly a century, and yet polls suggest
it's possible.
There's a trip to a conservative corner of Iowa.
That's a state where Democrats could flip the governor's office, three of four House
seats and the Senate seat because of how unpopular Republicans are.
Trump is visiting North Carolina as many Republican outside groups have basically gone dark on
the airwaves because the Senate race is viewed as a lost cause.
NPR Stephen Fowler reporting, while he was in Kansas yesterday, Trump offered farmers
a one-time payment.
It will help offset costly diesel prices.
The program will be about $8 billion in all, for farmers only.
The White House is launching a $25 million program to reward tipsters who report alleged
fraud to the U.S. government.
It's part of Vice President Vance's anti-fraud work.
NPR's Emily Feng reports it's also the Trump administration's response to mounting
voter concern about perceived government corruption.
A White House official told NPR that the announcement will be made in the Oval Office this afternoon.
The program will be run by the Department of Justice and would award up to $30,000 to
anyone who submits a tip that results in a successful fraud conviction.
Vance heads an anti-fraud task force that he claims has unearthed more than $260 billion
in fraud and federal spending since last January, though the task force has not provided data
for some of the claims, and at least one stems from a Biden-era investigation.
A recent Fox News poll this week found nearly 90 percent of Americans surveyed were concerned
about government corruption, even more than the percentage concerned about the economy.
Emily Feng and Pure News, the White House.
Mississippi officials have determined the fatal police shooting of a toddler was a justified
use of force.
From Mississippi Public Broadcasting and the Gulf States newsroom, Elise Katrina Gregg has
more.
One-year-old Cohen Wiley was shot in a Walmart parking lot in June after police responded
to a shoplifting call involving Wiley's mother and her friend.
The three were in a car that police claim was being driven towards them, which Wiley's
mother denies.
An officer then shot into the vehicle, killing Wiley.
Now the family's attorney, Van Turner, says the attorney general's findings that the shooting
was justified is "perplexing" and says they intend to pursue other means of legal recourse.
Since the county will not do it, the state will not do it, we're going to see, as federal
governors mention, to see if they'll be able to do something along with the civil action.
Wiley was only months away from his second birthday.
For NPR News, I'm Elise Katrina Gregg in Jackson, Mississippi.
This is NPR.
The FBI, the Postal Service and the U.S. Capitol Police are investigating dozens of letters
sent to lawmakers.
Some of the envelopes have suspicious substances.
They've turned up on Capitol Hill and local congressional offices around the country.
Some state elections offices, including Wisconsin, have also gotten them.
The latest envelope turned up yesterday at the local office of Virginia Democratic Congressman
Suhas Subramanyam.
There are no injuries reported.
North Korea has threatened, rather South Korea, has threatened decisive retaliation to any
military provocations by North Korea, and Piers Anthony Kuhn reports.
The South's Joint Chiefs of Staff says it instructed troops along the demilitarized
zone, or DMZ, to respond decisively to any incursions by North Korean troops.
On Monday, North Korean leader Kim Jong-un's sister Kim Yo-jong accused the South of broadcasting
warnings and firing warning shots at the North.
She said Pyongyang is considering resuming propaganda broadcasts, which were suspended
last year, and deploying more weapons along the DMZ.
Tensions have surged following a landmine blast in the DMZ last month, which injured
three South Korean soldiers.
There has been speculation that President Trump could meet with Kim Jong-un during a
summit in China next month.
But Trump told reporters he's unsure if anyone is requesting such a meeting.
Anthony Kuhn in PR News sold.
This year's World Series is set that Tampa Bay Rays beat the Cleveland Guardians last
night to clinch the American League pennant.
Tampa will now face the Milwaukee Brewers for the Fall Classic.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Trump campaigns in Kansas and North Carolina ahead of the midterm elections
Trump announces $8 billion one-time diesel relief payment for farmers
White House launches $25 million tipster program to report federal fraud, run by Justice Department
Mississippi officials rule fatal police shooting of 1-year-old Cohen Wiley justified
FBI, Postal Service and Capitol Police investigate suspicious letters sent to lawmakers
South Korea orders troops to respond decisively to North Korean incursions along DMZ
Tampa Bay Rays beat Cleveland Guardians to win American League pennant, face Milwaukee Brewers
